items.subject: Torah & Tanakh
items.prompt: Without options: when a narrative repeats a description, what is your first reading move?
accepted: ask how the repetition shapes the meaning
notice the repetition and ask how it shapes meaning
items.model: Notice the repetition, then ask how it shapes the source's literary and emotional force.

items.subject: Tefillah
items.prompt: Name the function of a line that asks God for healing.
items.model: It is a petition: a direct request within the structure of prayer.

items.subject: Halakha
items.prompt: Complete the study boundary: Seder maps sources and reasoning; a real-life ruling may require…
items.model: …qualified guidance and context. Learning a chain is not the same as receiving a personal ruling.

items.subject: Jewish Thought
items.prompt: When two thinkers share a source but disagree, name two things you should compare.
items.model: Compare their concepts, claims, and reasons—then identify the precise point of divergence.

items.subject: Mussar & Chassidus
items.prompt: Complete the reflection sequence: source, trait, and…
items.model: A small practice. Ethical reflection should be source-grounded, modest, and revisitable.

items.subject: Jewish History
items.prompt: Give two historical questions to ask before drawing conclusions from a source.
accepted: who is the audience and what does it claim
who is it for and what does it claim
who is addressed and what does it claim
items.model: Ask what it claims, who it addresses, what setting it comes from, and what kind of evidence it is.

items.subject: Judaism & the Wider World
items.prompt: Complete the comparative method: shared question, context, similarity, and…
items.model: Difference. Responsible comparison names a real connection without erasing distinct sources and settings.
